subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files

question: Should `wiki apply synthesis --body-file` gain a fixed 1 MiB rejection limit, and if so what supported upgrade contract should apply to existing larger inputs?
rationale: The current implementation and documentation expose no size ceiling, so selecting a permanent rejection threshold is a user-visible compatibility policy rather than a mechanical bug repair.

options.title: Approve a documented cap
options.body: Adopt an owner-selected limit, document it as the command contract, and require live evidence for accepted and rejected files before merge.

options.title: Preserve existing input capacity
options.body: Replace the hard rejection with an implementation that avoids unsafe buffering while continuing to accept previously valid large inputs.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Close or defer the PR if neither a bounded compatibility design nor a justified public limit is currently wanted.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing input capacity
recommendation.body: Replace the hard rejection with an implementation that avoids unsafe buffering while continuing to accept previously valid large inputs.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the wiki apply CLI surface whose large-file behavior this PR would change.
